name: Keelwright Freight
tagline: A mid-size freight-logistics platform: quoting, booking, carrier integrations, tracking and billing for shippers in North America, and since 2025, Europe.
profile: AWS (us-east-1, eu-central-1 since 2025), Postgres on RDS, Redis, Kafka on MSK, Keycloak
Markdown ADRs in each team's repository; postmortems for SEV-1/2; change notes in Slack and ops reviews
problem: Keelwright writes ADRs, but the conditions behind them change in other documents written by other people: a capacity review, a Slack announcement, a postmortem. Nobody re-reads a 2023 ADR when finance moves reporting to Snowflake in 2025. Teams keep copying decisions whose reasons have expired.

story.text: Payments picks PostgreSQL for the ledger because finance runs month-end SQL JOINs directly on it and writes stay under ~1,800/s (ADR-007).
Pricing caches quotes in one us-east-1 Redis cluster: every shipper is in North America (ADR-012).
Integrations adds 5 retries with exponential backoff to carrier calls: failures look transient (ADR-027).
Retry storm against Northline's rate limit takes bookings down for 47 minutes (PM-2024-11).
EU launch: shippers in Germany, the Netherlands and Poland, priced in EUR (SIG-2025-01).
EU shippers get stale, wrong-currency quotes from the us-east-1 cache (PM-2025-02).
Jin Park moves to Payments; Marcus is the only Kafka operator left (SIG-2025-05).
Finance moves month-end close to Snowflake; direct queries on the ledger are disabled (SIG-2025-08).
Cyber Monday: ledger writes peak at 3,140/s (SIG-2025-12).
Enterprise deals now require SOC 2 Type II (SIG-2026-02).
Invoice batch overruns its window at 340k invoices a night (SIG-2026-05).
A new team building the customs-duty ledger asks: 'Postgres, like payments did?'

dataset.distractors: 16 routine change notes (CI migrations, upgrades, on-call changes) and 2 unrelated ADRs, so retrieval has to find the relevant change among noise
construction: ADRs follow the MADR template in prose; assumptions are never listed, only implied in Context, as in real ADRs.
Change notes never name the decision they invalidate (STALE's 'implicit conflict').
Every record has a real-looking author, date, numbers and, for postmortems, log excerpts.
At least one decision still fully holds (ADR-019), so REUSE is a real outcome.
Hand-labelled gold assumptions with verbatim quotes live only in evaluation/, never in the corpus.
